## Historical audit — S0135

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/generic_rsi/C2/test/commons_199974832/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 2 of 3 is visible; citations below refer to its JSONL lines and supplied character ranges.

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal and scene | The student was instructed to reconstruct a 512 × 384 indoor photograph with separate editable meshes and matched camera, occlusion and materials. The student interpreted it as a woodworking tool room; that semantic interpretation is not independent image verification. Code includes walls, window, shelves, workbench, numerous planes, tools and containers (line 13, `model_request`, chars [0,206551)). |
| Geometry and pose | The programs group components into assets, including a solid bench top and apron, plane bodies and handles, and open measuring-tool arms. Individual tools are rotated and placed; camera pose and lens are explicit. Grouping and coordinates do not establish physical connection, support, correct pose or reference correspondence (lines 13 and 16, chars [0,206551) and [0,15227)). |
| First revision | After step 1 reported a render, the student estimated shelf and bowl landmarks, diagnosed pale surfaces and changed lens 31→36, extended walls to address a claimed sky band, and transferred diffuse colors to shader nodes. Step 2 also reported `ok: true` and `render_available`. These are student diagnoses and executed changes, not independently verified improvements (line 13, chars [0,206551)). |
| Second revision | After receiving step 2 feedback, the student estimated framing was close but wood and iron remained pale. The response darkened palette values and implemented explicit named-primitive material assignment with procedural wood noise and metallic settings, while retaining camera and lights. The runner executed that program as step 3 (lines 15–16, chars [0,14585) and [0,15227)). |
| Validation and selection | Step 3 returned `ok: true`, empty stderr, and a saved render and Blender scene; the next event selected step 3 (lines 17–18, chars [0,83310) and [0,59)). This is **formal execution/render success**, not proof of visual or geometric correctness. No independent comparison or final evaluation is visible here. |
| Teacher and exploration | No separate teacher message, teacher detection, diagnosis or proposed update appears in this chunk; receipt or adoption cannot be established. The student did respond to runner instructions and successive render feedback. The fresh third CLI session had three images supplied, was read-only with tools disabled, and recorded zero tool calls; its response was subsequently executed by the runner (lines 13–16, cited ranges; line 14 chars [0,3804)). |

**Lessons and uncertainty.** Transferable: distinguish a successful render from verified fidelity, and trace proposed material or camera corrections through execution. Task-specific: the pale-finish and sky-band diagnoses motivated changes here, but their causes and effectiveness remain hypotheses without the images. The code specifies multiple objects, wood/metal treatments, camera and lighting, but neither image pixels nor geometric tests are available to this audit; actual visibility, occlusion, texture appearance, part contacts and lighting quality remain unknown. Other chunks and any later outcome are not inferred.
